messages.subject: error output from ezPredict
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I get the following error when I try to run ezPredict on my data set after running lmer() in lme4.

contrasts(this_fixed_data) : contrasts apply only to factors

I think I am running lme4 version 1.1-7.

To see if I could remedy the situation by running a different (earlier) version of lmer, I installed lme4.0 and ran lmer again.  But this time I get a different error:

Error in UseMethod("fixef") :
  no applicable method for 'fixef' applied to an object of class "mer"

Any help would be tremendously appreciated.

Sincerely,
K. Tajima

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] error output from ezPredict
messages.body_plain:
Are you supplying a value to the "to_predict" argument to ezPredict?
If so I wonder if you have forgotten to factorize columns in that data
frame that were factors in the data frame that was used to create the
model from which you are attempting to derive predictions.

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] error output from ezPredict
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mike,

Thank you for your quick reply, and sorry for the delayed response on my part.

> Are you supplying a value to the "to_predict" argument to ezPredict?

No, I am simply passing the fitted lmer object, without any further arguments to ezPredict, as below.

preds <- ezPredict(data)

The odd thing is, I have asked a colleague to run the same script as mine on his platform, using the same data, running R 3.0.2 and lme4 (0.999999-2).  But he did not get an error from ezPredict.

On my platform, I run R 3.0.2, and probably the latest version of lme4, and get the aforementioned error.

So I wonder if it has something to do with compatibility between ez and (latest) versions of lme4.  Are you aware of issues like this?  If yes, are there ways to get around them?

Thank you in advance for any input.

Sincerely,
K. Tajima
